content:
maya: seeing a sudden spike of 502/504s hitting hosted inference since ~10:05 UTC. Multiple customers, different regions. sample trace id: trace-0a1b2c3d. A few requests return partial tokens then cut.
chris: which upstreams? envoy logs or edge proxy traces?
jordan: envoy shows a lot of \"upstream reset before response\" and \"stream reset\" errors. snippet:
```
[envoy] [warning] stream 12345: upstream reset: connection failure (upstream response not received)
upstream cluster: api-models-quant, response_code: 502
```
maya: repro curl I used (no creds):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwdl-7b-q","input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
response often: 502 with body \"upstream closed connection\" or a partial stream then ECONNRESET.
chris: any recent config/deploys? auth / rate limit / cache changes?
deploy-bot: deployment completed 1799990800 by chris: "auth-cache: use sharded TTL eviction + reconnect backoff" -> revision: auth-cache-v2.3
sre-oncall: seeing auth-kv (redis) p95 spikes to 700-900ms starting at 10:03 UTC. Envoy health checks for api-models clusters started transiently marking hosts unhealthy which increases connection churn.
maya: interesting — some requests hit a fallback path that tries to refresh auth token synchronously and blocks on auth-kv. when that blocks, the upstream connection pool saturates and streams reset.
jordan: logs show repeated \"connect() to backend timed out\" and \"connection reuse disabled\" entries. also a handful of \"http/2 stream head hit max window\" warnings.
chris: hypothesize: auth-cache eviction loop + slow kv = blocking auth middleware -> backpressure on worker threadpool -> long-lived connections from edge -> envoy resets when upstream doesn't respond. matches 502s and partial streams.
support-bot: customer tickets opened: #CUST-9384 (high severity), #CUST-9390; customers reported yesterday they saw partial completions and app-level retries intensified the issue.
maya: mitigation applied: 1) rolled back auth-cache eviction change at 1799991180, 2) temporarily increased auth-kv replica pool + turned on local in-memory fallback, 3) bumped envoy upstream connection limit for api-models cluster. after ~2m we saw 502 rate drop.
chris: can we capture exact timeline for correlation (deploy -> p95 auth -> envoy health -> customer 502s)? put traces into SRE dashboard and correlate with deploy id.
jordan: saved sample traces (trace-0a1b2c3d, trace-0f9e8d7c). will attach flame graphs and envoy logs to the incident ticket.
sre-oncall: next steps: add a guarded async auth refresh (so auth-kv latency can't stall request threads), add circuit breaker on auth-kv TTL churn, increase observability on prefix cache queue lengths. also schedule a postmortem.
maya: customer update draft: "we identified an auth-cache regression that caused backend saturation and intermittent 502s. we've rolled back the change and added mitigations. we'll follow up with a postmortem and timeline." :white_check_mark:
jordan: assigning follow-ups: chris -> revert permanent plan + qa; dev infra -> add auth-kv circuit breaker; docs -> update runbook for auth-cache regressions.
chris: thanks all. closing interim incident once last 10m looks clean, will keep watch for 1 hour.
